An ideal 5-stage pipeline with no stalls executes 200 instructions in how many cycles?
mcq.e: Total cycles = k + n - 1 = 5 + 200 - 1 = 204. 205 forgets the overlap of the first stage; 1000 is the unpipelined 5 x 200.

mcq.q: For 100 instructions on a 5-stage pipeline, what is the speedup over an unpipelined machine taking 5 cycles per instruction (stalls ignored)?
mcq.e: Unpipelined = 500 cycles, pipelined = 104 cycles, so 500/104 is about 4.8. The ideal speedup of 5 (number of stages) is only approached as n becomes very large.

mcq.q: A program is 90% parallelizable. What is the maximum possible speedup by Amdahl's Law, however many processors are used?
mcq.e: Maximum speedup with infinite S is 1/(1-P) = 1/0.1 = 10. The serial 10% always remains.

mcq.q: By Amdahl's Law, what is the overall speedup if 50% of a program is sped up by 10x?
mcq.e: Speedup = 1/((1-0.5) + 0.5/10) = 1/0.55 = about 1.82. 2.0x is only the ceiling 1/(1-P) reached when S is infinite.

mcq.q: A 3 GHz CPU executes 6 x 10^9 instructions with an average CPI of 1.5. How long does the program take?
mcq.e: Cycles = 6e9 x 1.5 = 9e9; time = 9e9 / 3e9 Hz = 3 s. 2 s would result from ignoring CPI.

mcq.q: A cache has a hit time of 1 ns, a miss rate of 5%, and a miss penalty of 80 ns. What is the AMAT?
mcq.e: AMAT = hit time + miss rate x miss penalty = 1 + 0.05 x 80 = 5 ns. 4 ns is only the miss term.

mcq.q: A memory has 14 address lines and 16-bit words. What is its capacity?
mcq.e: 2^14 = 16,384 words x 2 bytes = 32,768 bytes = 32 KB. 16 KB would be correct only for 8-bit words.

mcq.q: How many address lines are needed to address every byte of a 2 MB memory?
mcq.e: 2 MB = 2^21 bytes, so 21 lines. 20 lines reach only 1 MB (the 8086 limit).

mcq.q: The practical (implemented) address width of 64-bit x86-64 CPUs of the era in the notes, 48 bits, gives an address space of:
mcq.e: 2^48 bytes = 256 TB. 16 EB is the theoretical limit of a full 64-bit address (2^64).

mcq.q: Approximately what bandwidth does a PCIe Gen 4 x4 link provide (about 2 GB/s per lane)?
mcq.e: 4 lanes x ~2 GB/s = ~8 GB/s, which is why Gen 4 NVMe SSDs peak near 7 GB/s. Bandwidth per lane doubles each generation.

mcq.q: Which technique removes a RAW (read-after-write) data hazard in a pipeline without always stalling?
mcq.e: Forwarding passes a result straight from the EX/MEM stage to the dependent instruction. Branch prediction and delay slots address control hazards; a second memory port addresses structural hazards.

mcq.q: Register renaming removes which hazards?
mcq.e: WAR and WAW are name dependences caused by reusing register names, which renaming eliminates. RAW is a true data dependence and cannot be renamed away.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the three classic types of cache miss?
mcq.e: The three Cs are compulsory, capacity and conflict. Associativity is a mapping scheme, not a miss type.

mcq.q: Which cache write policy marks lines with a dirty bit and updates main memory only when the line is evicted?
mcq.e: Write-back defers the memory update using a dirty bit. Write-through updates memory on every write; write-allocate only decides whether a block is loaded into cache on a write miss.

mcq.q: How many logical processors does an 8-core CPU with 2-way SMT (Hyper-Threading) present to the OS?
mcq.e: SMT runs 2 threads per core, so 8 x 2 = 16 logical processors, though not 16 times the performance.

mcq.q: Which flash type is typically used for firmware code storage, while the other is used in SSDs, USB drives and SD cards?
mcq.e: NOR flash allows random-access reads suited to executing firmware code; NAND is dense and used for bulk storage. EEPROM and mask ROM are different ROM-family types.

mcq.q: Which ROM type is erased by exposing the chip to ultraviolet light?
mcq.e: EPROM uses a UV-transparent window for erasure. EEPROM is erased electrically, PROM is one-time programmable, and mask ROM is fixed at manufacture.

mcq.q: A 32-bit value 0x12345678 is stored starting at address 0x100 on a big-endian machine. What byte is at address 0x101?
mcq.e: Big-endian puts the most significant byte first: 0x100=12, 0x101=34, 0x102=56, 0x103=78. On little-endian, 0x101 would hold 0x56.

mcq.q: In IEEE 754 single precision, the stored exponent field is 130. What is the true exponent?
mcq.e: The exponent bias is 127, so the true exponent = 130 - 127 = 3. (Double precision uses a bias of 1023.)

mcq.q: What is the range of an 8-bit two's complement integer?
mcq.e: Two's complement has one extra negative value: -128 to +127. -127 to 127 is the range of sign-magnitude or one's complement; 0 to 255 is unsigned.

mcq.q: Which signed number representations each have two representations of zero (+0 and -0)?
mcq.e: Sign-magnitude and 1's complement both have +0 and -0; 2's complement has a single zero, which is one reason it is used for signed integers.

mcq.q: Which status flag is set when an unsigned addition produces a carry out of the most significant bit?
mcq.e: The carry flag signals unsigned carry/borrow. The overflow flag signals signed two's complement overflow, which is a different condition.

mcq.q: During the fetch step, which sequence of register transfers is correct?
mcq.a: PC to MAR, memory to MDR, MDR to IR, PC incremented
w: PC to MDR, memory to MAR, MAR to IR, PC incremented
IR to MAR, memory to PC, MDR to IR
PC to IR, IR to MAR, memory to MDR
mcq.e: The PC supplies the address via MAR, the instruction comes back through MDR into the IR, and the PC is advanced to the next instruction.

mcq.q: Which technique relies on the compiler to pack independent operations into one long instruction word for parallel issue?
mcq.e: VLIW (and Intel's EPIC/Itanium) shifts parallelism detection to compile time. Superscalar, out-of-order and SMT find parallelism in hardware at run time.

mcq.q: A system has four 2 TB drives in RAID 5. What is the usable capacity?
mcq.e: RAID 5 gives up one drive's worth for parity: (4 - 1) x 2 TB = 6 TB. 4 TB would be RAID 6 or RAID 10; 8 TB would be RAID 0.

mcq.q: Which RAID level can guarantee survival of any two simultaneous drive failures?
mcq.e: RAID 6 uses double parity. RAID 5 tolerates one failure; RAID 10 survives two only if they hit different mirror pairs, so it is not guaranteed.

mcq.q: A disk has 2 surfaces, 1024 tracks per surface, 64 sectors per track and 512 bytes per sector. What is its capacity?
How many 16K x 4-bit chips are needed to build a 64K x 8-bit memory?
mcq.e: Depth: 64K/16K = 4 banks; width: 8/4 = 2 chips per bank; 4 x 2 = 8 chips.

mcq.q: Which Flynn class is rare and associated mainly with fault-tolerant systems?
mcq.e: MISD applies multiple instruction streams to the same data and is mostly seen in redundant fault-tolerant designs. Multicore and clusters are MIMD; GPUs and vector units are SIMD.

mcq.q: Which NIST post-quantum standard (FIPS 203) specifies the key-encapsulation mechanism formerly known as Kyber?
mcq.e: ML-KEM is FIPS 203 (Kyber). ML-DSA (FIPS 204, Dilithium) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205, SPHINCS+) are digital signature standards.
